question: In paraquat poisoning, supplemental high-flow oxygen should be given early to support respiration and prevent hypoxia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Paraquat's mechanism of toxicity depends on generating superoxide radicals using available O₂; supplemental oxygen fuels the reaction and accelerates the fatal pulmonary fibrosis. This is one of the most important and counterintuitive rules in clinical toxicology.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Oxygen is CONTRAINDICATED in paraquat poisoning. Paraquat generates superoxide free radicals using O₂ in lung tissue. Supplemental oxygen dramatically accelerates this free-radical cascade, worsening pulmonary fibrosis. O₂ is only used when SpO₂ falls below ~40%.
